summary: C-0002: There is NO hypnosis-specific, unique physiological 'fingerprint'; induction effects are small and expectancy/hypnotizability often matter more — supports non-state / sociocognitive interpretation
content: CLAIM C-0002: Across multiple 2023-2025 sources, no robust neurophysiological signature UNIQUE to hypnosis has been identified. EEG spectral power (theta/alpha/gamma) was not time-locked to induction in highly hypnotizable participants when expectancy was controlled (2023). BIS/CSI monitors confirm 'neurophysiological correlates of hypnosis but no hypnosis-specific fingerprint' (2023). 54% of participants are equally or less suggestible after induction (Braffman & Kirsch 1999, cited in Lynn/Kirsch/Terhune 2023). A preregistered Stroop study found Bayesian equivalence between posthypnotic suggestion and volitional request (Dienes et al.). Social-cognitive theorists conclude neurophysiological data do NOT resolve the altered-state issue. SUPPORTS: non-state interpretation. LIMIT: 'no unique fingerprint yet' is not the same as 'no real state exists' (absence of evidence problem).
